title: STATISTICS ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to ensure reliability of statistics and efficiency in operating statistical systems by prescribing matters necessary for producing, disseminating, and using statistics, and laying the foundation therefor, etc.

Article 2 (Fundamental concepts) (1) Statistics shall be produced, disseminated, and used in a manner that contributes to the development of society as a public resource to help rational decision-making.
  (2) Statistics shall be produced in a scientific manner in order to ensure accuracy, timeliness, consistency, and impartiality. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016>
  (3) Statistics shall be widely disseminated and used insofar as the confidentiality of the relevant individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. is guaranteed.

Article 3 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Apr. 1, 2009; Dec. 18, 2012; Jan. 27, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020; Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. "Statistics" means any numerical information produced directly by a statistics service agency or by commissioning or entrusting to another agency, corporation, organization, etc. (hereinafter "agency, etc.") concerning specific group, object, etc., such as industry, commodity price, population, housing, culture and environment, for the purpose of utilizing it in formulating and evaluating government policies or in researching and analyzing socio-economic phenomena or for other purposes; provided, the numerical information prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as any numerical information produced for internal purposes by a statistics service agency, shall be excluded herefrom;
  2. "Designated statistics" means statistics that the Minister of Data and Statistics designates and publicly notifies under Article 17;
  3. "Statistics service agency" means a central administrative agency, local government or a statistics service agency designated under Article 15;
  3-2; "Statistical register" means materials managed by the Minister of Data and Statistics which contains basic information by field on the population of individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. of statistical data and administrative data in order to support the production of statistics by statistics service agencies;
  4. "Statistical data" means data that a statistics service agency has collected, acquired, or used to produce statistics (including computer data, such as database), excluding statistical registers;
  5. "Public institution" means any of the following central administrative agencies, local governments or other institutions:
  a. Public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
  b. Local government-invested public corporations or local government public corporations under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
  c. Various levels of schools established pursuant to the Early Childhood Education Act, the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Higher Education Act, and other statutes;
  d. Special corporations established under special Acts;
  e. A centralized credit information collection agency that obtains permission from the Financial Services Commission pursuant to Article 25 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act;
  6. "Statistics staff" means persons engaging in business affairs relating to the production or dissemination of statistical data at a statistics service agency;
  7. "Administrative data" means, other than statistical registers and statistical data, documents, ledgers, and drawings, and other computer data, including database, which are officially prepared, acquired, and managed by public institutions.

Article 4 (Responsibilities of the State) (1) The State and local governments shall formulate and implement policies necessary to realize the purpose and basic principles of this Act.
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall collectively coordinate and maintain matters regarding statistics and devise measures to expand the production, dissemination and use of statistics so that statistics may contribute to the development of the society. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The heads of statistics service agencies shall endeavor to minimize burden and protect confidentiality for individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "statistical respondents") who provide answers to inquiries, submit data upon request, etc., in order to produce statistics.
  (4) Heads of statistics service agencies shall cooperate with one another for the exchange of statistics staff, joint research and development of statistics production techniques, sharing of statistical data, etc. <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012>
  (5) The head of a statistics service agency shall actively endeavor to improve the treatment of statistics staff, enhance their welfare, improve their status, and create a safe environment for statistics staff to conduct on-site investigations. <Added on Mar. 26, 2024>

Article 4-2 (Statistics day) The State shall designate September 1 as the Statistics Day and hold commemorative events annually in order to raise public awareness of the importance of statistics and promote the use of statistics.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 1, 2009]

Article 5 (Relationship to Other Statutes) (1) Except as otherwise provided in other statutes, the production, dissemination and use of statistics shall be governed by this Act.
  (2) When the head of a related administrative agency intends to legislate, amend, or repeal any statute that contains provisions regarding the production, dissemination, and use of statistics, he or she shall have a prior consultation with the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

CHAPTER II PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION OF STATISTICS AND CONSTRUCTION OF BASIS FOR USE THEREOF

Article 5-2 (National Statistics Committee) (1) A National Statistics Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established under the control of the Minister of Economy and Finance to deliberate and resolve on matters relating to the production, dissemination, and use of statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Committee shall deliberate and resolve on the following matters: <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012; Jul. 18, 2023>
  1. Mid- and long-term policy goals for the development of national statistics and directions for the promotion thereof;
  2. Matters regarding the formulation and modification of a master plan and implementation plans for the development of national statistics referred to in Articles 5-5 and 5-6;
  3. Matters regarding the adjustment and consolidation of similar and overlapping statistics and the cooperation among statistics service agencies;
  4. Matters regarding quality control, such as checkup and improvement of the quality of statistics;
  5. Matters regarding the standards for production, dissemination and use of statistics, such as standard classification of statistics;
  6. Matters regarding the utilization of administrative materials;
  7. Matters regarding the utilization of statistical information systems of statistics service agencies referred to in Article 7-2;
  8. Other matters regarding the production, dissemination, and use of statistics, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The Committee shall be composed of up to 30 members, including 1 Chairperson; and the Minister of Economy and Finance shall be the Chairperson. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Matters necessary for the organization, management, etc. of the Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 5-3 (Establishment and operation of statistical registers) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics may establish and operate statistical registers for each field, such as population, housing, and business entities, to support statistics service agencies in producing statistics efficiently. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The statistics register shall be established based on administrative data, statistical data, data collected through on-site investigations under Article 26(4), and other data prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the establishment and operation of statistical registers, such as types of statistical registers, items to be established for each type, and methods of establishment, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree
  [This Article Added on Jul. 18, 2023]
  [Previous Article 5-3 moved to Article 5-4 <Jul. 18, 2023>]

Article 5-4 (Conducting census) (1) In order to produce basic statistics to be utilized as basic data for policy-making and collection of various kinds of statistical data, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall take a complete enumeration of population, housing, business entities, etc. across the nation (hereinafter referred to as "census"). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Matters necessary for the scope, method, etc. of census shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]
  [Moved from Article 5-3; previous Article 5-4 moved to Article 5-5 <Jul. 18, 2023>]

Article 5-5 (Formulation of implementation plans for development of national statistics) (1) The Government shall set mid- and long-term policy goals for the development of national statistics and directions for the promotion thereof, and formulate and promote a master plan for the development of national statistics based thereon (hereinafter referred to as "master plan").
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall prepare a master plan every five years in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, Do Governors and Governors of Special Self-Governing Provinces (including superintendents of education and hereinafter referred to as "Mayors/Do Governors"), and finalize the master plan through deliberation and resolution of the Committee. The same shall apply where he or she intends to alter the finalized master plan. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The following matters shall be included in the master plan:
  1. Mid- and long-term policy goals for the development of national statistics and directions for the promotion thereof;
  2. Major tasks to be implemented in each term and methods for the implementation;
  3. Scale of financial resources required and methods for financing;
  4. Other matters deemed necessary for the development of national statistics.
  (4) Matters necessary for formulation procedures of the master plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Upon formulating the master plan, the Government shall submit it to the National Assembly without delay.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]
  [Moved from Article 5-4; previous Article 5-5 moved to Article 5-6 <Jul. 18, 2023>]

Article 5-6 (Formulation of implementation plans for development of national statistics) (1) When the Minister of Data and Statistics has formulated a master plan, he or she shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors thereof, and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors shall formulate an annual action plan according to the notified master plan each year and submit it to the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall formulate an annual implementation plan for the development of national statistics (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") each year after receiving an annual action plan based on the master plan from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for formulation procedures of the implementation plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]
  [Moved from Article 5-5 <Jul. 18, 2023>]

Article 6 (Designation and management of staff in charge of statistics) (1) The heads of statistics service agencies shall designate and manage a staff member in charge of statistics from among the staff under their control, and have him or her exercise general supervision over the following business affairs relating to the production, dissemination and use of statistics under their jurisdiction. In such cases, the scope of a person subject to designation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Mar. 31, 2010>
  1. Business affairs relating to integration, coordination and quality control of statistics of the statistics service agency and its affiliated agency;
  2. Business affairs relating to cooperation with other statistics service agencies;
  3. Business affairs relating to the production and distribution of gender statistics classified by gender if natural persons are included in statistics;
  4. Other business affairs relating to the production, dissemination, and use of statistics under their jurisdiction.
  (2) The heads of statistics service agencies shall notify the Minister of Data and Statistics without delay when they have designated or changed any staff in charge of statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 7 (Securing of human resources and budget of statistics service agency) (1) The heads of statistics service agencies shall strive to secure human resources and budget necessary for the production and dissemination of statistics.
  (2) Where the Minister of Data and Statistics finds that the statistics service agencies significantly lack human resources and budget necessary for the production and dissemination of statistics, he or she may recommend the head of such statistics service agencies to secure necessary human resources and budget. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 7-2 (Establishment and operation of statistical information systems) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall establish and operate statistical information systems to enable statistics service agencies to efficiently produce, disseminate and use statistical data following standardized processes. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics may recommend statistics service agencies to use statistical information systems under paragraph (1) after deliberation by the Committee. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]

Article 8 (Statistics education and establishment of basic plans for statistics education) (1) In order to improve the quality of statistics staff, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall endeavor to conduct statistics education. <Amended on Mar. 31, 2010; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics may develop and implement a basic plan for statistics education which contains a comprehensive and systematic education schedule, courses and other relevant matters to effectively conduct education under paragraph (1). <Added on Mar. 31, 2010; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The heads of statistics service agencies shall actively cooperate in conducting education under paragraph (1) and statistics staff shall actively participate in such education. <Amended on Mar. 31, 2010>
  (4) The Minister of Data and Statistics may recommend the heads of statistics service agencies to conduct their own in-house education on statistics. <Amended on Mar. 31, 2010; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) The scope of persons to be educated, curricula of education and other necessary matters under paragraphs (1) and (4) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 31, 2010>
  [Title Amended on Mar. 31, 2010]

Article 9 (Regular examinations of quality of statistics) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall periodically conduct an examination of the quality of statistics (hereinafter referred to as "regular examinations of the quality of statistics") concerning the entire process of production and dissemination of major statistical data prescribed by Presidential Decree, which are widely used for the formulation and evaluation of various kinds of policies of the Government or for the production of other statistical data, within the scope of ten years. <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall formulate a plan of regular examination of the quality of statistics, including the following matters and shall notify the heads of statistics service agencies by the end of February of the year when the regular examination of the quality of statistics is conducted: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Statistics subject to regular examinations of the quality of statistics;
  2. Timing and methods for regular examinations of the quality of statistics;
  3. Plans for utilizing results of regular examinations of the quality of statistics;
  4. Other matters necessary to conduct regular examinations of the quality of statistics.
  (3) The regular examinations of the quality of statistics shall be conducted by such methods as requesting submission of data under Article 35, visiting statistics service agencies for confirmation and on-site verification of statistical respondents.
  (4) The Minister of Data and Statistics may exempt statistics from the regular examinations of the quality of statistics if the occasional examination of the quality of statistics under Article 10 is being conducted on such statistics or has been conducted on such statistics during a period prescribed by Presidential Decree, or if such statistics are found by the self-examination of the quality of statistics under Article 11 to be of excellent quality. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) When the Minister of Data and Statistics completes a regular examination of the quality of statistics, he or she shall notify the heads of statistics service agencies of the results without delay. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (6) Matters necessary for the formulation of a plan of regular examination of the quality of statistics, and cycle, methods and procedures of regular examinations of the quality of statistics, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012>

Article 10 (Occasional examinations of quality of statistics) (1) As occasion requires, the Minister of Data and Statistics may examine the quality of statistics (hereinafter referred to as "occasional examination of the quality of statistics") regarding which there are reasons to believe that the self-examination of the quality of statistics under Article 11 has not been conducted or that the quality thereof has declined. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) When the Minister of Data and Statistics conducts an occasional examination of the quality of statistics, he or she shall notify the relevant statistics service agency of the reason, time, method, etc. of an occasional examination of the quality of statistics in advance. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Article 9(3) and (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to occasional examinations of the quality of statistics.
  (4) Matters necessary for the methods, procedures, etc. for occasional examinations of the quality of statistics shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Self-examinations of quality of statistics) (1) The heads of statistics service agencies shall examine the quality of the statistics under their jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as "self-examination of the quality of statistics") each year; provided, as for the statistics whose frequency of production exceeds one year, it may be conducted in the year when the statistics are produced or in years thereafter.
  (2) When the heads of statistics service agencies have conducted a regular examination of the quality of statistics or occasional examination of the quality of statistics, they need not conduct self-examination of the quality of statistics of the year.
  (3) The heads of statistics service agencies shall submit the result of self-examination of the quality of statistics to the Minister of Data and Statistics by December 31 of the year in which it was conducted. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Matters necessary for the methods, procedures, etc. for self-examination of the quality of statistics shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Request for improvement of production and dissemination of statistics) (1) If it is recognized necessary to secure the reliability of statistics and the efficiency of operation of the statistics system, such as reflection of the results of regular examinations of the quality of statistics, of occasional examinations of the quality of statistics or of self-examinations of the quality of statistics, and the coordination of similar or overlapping statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the heads of statistics service agencies to suspend or change the production of statistics or to improve the business affairs relating to the production and dissemination of statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) When the head of a statistic service agency receives a request under paragraph (1), he or she shall comply therewith unless there is good cause. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>

Article 12-2 (Statistics-based policy evaluation) (1) If the head of a central administrative agency introduces a new policy or system by enacting or revising statutes within his or her jurisdiction or changes significant matters of the former policies and systems, he or she shall request the Minister of Data and Statistics to evaluate the existence or non-existence, etc. of statistical data appropriate for the execution and evaluation of the policies and systems to be introduced or changed (hereinafter referred to as "statistics-based policy evaluation"); provided, this shall not apply in any of the following cases: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Matters regarding national security;
  2. Matters regarding administrative proceedings and administrative organizations;
  3. Matters regarding procedures, trials, and execution of punishment in civil, commercial, and criminal litigations;
  4. Other matters that the Minister of Data and Statistics determines to be inappropriate for statistics-based policy evaluation.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request under paragraph (1), the Minister of Data and Statistics shall evaluate whether the policies and systems are based on statistical data and notify the head of the relevant central administrative agency of his or her opinions, including the appropriateness or inappropriateness of the statistical data related to the policies and systems and plans for the development and improvement of statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The head of a central administrative agency shall present the relevant bill to a cabinet meeting, along with the opinion of evaluation of the Minister of Data and Statistics under paragraph (2). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall formulate guidelines for statistics-based policy evaluation and notify the heads of central administrative agencies thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) Matters necessary for methods, procedures, etc. of statistics-based policy evaluation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]

Article 13 (Subsidization of expenses and provision of advice and technical assistance) (1) For the purposes of development of statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may provide subsidies to cover part of the expenses incurred in the operation and business of statistics service agencies or the agencies, etc. that conduct business concerning the education, development, promotion, diagnosis of quality, or public relations of statistics within the budget every year, and if it is deemed necessary for the production and dissemination of statistics, he or she may provide advice or technical assistance. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) If the Minister of Data and Statistics is requested by the heads of statistics service agencies to provide advice or technical assistance necessary for the production and dissemination of statistics, he or she shall actively cooperate. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [Title Amended on Jul. 18, 2023]

Article 14 (International cooperation) For the purposes of development of statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may perform the following with international organizations, foreign governments, or foreign organizations: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Joint study of production and analysis of statistics and development of statistics;
  2. Passing down or inheriting the techniques of production of statistics thereto or therefrom;
  3. Training of foreign statistics staff;
  4. Technical assistance, and passing down or inheriting techniques;
  5. Exchanges and cooperation.

Article 14-2 (Monitoring of statistics provided to international organizations) (1) The head of a statistics service agency may provide international organizations with statistics.
  (2) The head of a statistics service agency shall monitor the status and utilization of the statistics being provided under paragraph (1), prepare a report thereon, and submit it to the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for the provision of statistics under paragraph (1), monitoring, submission of a report, etc. under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 27, 2016]

CHAPTER III DESIGNATION OF DESIGNATED STATISTICS SERVICE AGENCIES AND DESIGNATED STATISTICS

Article 15 (Designation of designated statistics service agencies) (1) In cases of a request from an agency, etc. which produces or intends to produce numerical information that is used in the formulation and evaluation of government policies or in the research, analysis, etc. of economic and social phenomena, the Minister of Data and Statistics may designate the agency, etc. concerned as a designated statistics service agency for the purposes of development of statistics. In such cases, the requirements for designation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of statistics production organization, budget, plans for statistics production, etc. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Where a public institution (excluding central administrative agencies or local governments) that produces numerical information used in the formulation and evaluation of government policies or in the research, analysis, etc. of economic and social phenomena does not apply for designation under paragraph (1), the Minister of Data and Statistics may designate it as a designated statistics service agency through deliberation and resolution by the Committee. <Amended on Dec. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for the application for designation of designated statistics service agencies, procedures, methods, etc. of designation thereof shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Revocation of designation of designated statistics service agency) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics may revoke the designation of a designated statistics service agency if the agency falls within any of the following cases: <Amended on Dec. 27, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where the head of a statistics service agency fails to comply with a request for suspension of or change in production of statistics or with a request for improvement of business affairs relating to the production and dissemination of statistics, in violation of Article 12(2);
  2. Where it ceases to meet the requirements for designation under the latter part of Article 15(1);
  2-2. Where the head of a designated statistics service agency that is a public institution (excluding central administrative agencies or local governments) requests revocation of designation as a designated statistics service agency;
  3. Where it has produced new statistics, suspended production of statistics, or changed approved matters without obtaining approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 18(1);
  4. Where it has produced new statistics, suspended production of statistics, or changed consulted matters without obtaining approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 20(1);
  5. Where it fails to comply with a request for submission of data by the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 35(2).
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall revoke the designation of a designated statistics service agency in any of the following cases; provided, where the head of a statistics service agency submits a plan for the production of new statistics in cases falling under subparagraph 2, such revocation may be deferred as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Dec. 27, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where the head of such designated statistics service agency that is not a public institution requests revocation of its designation as a designated statistics service agency;
  2. Where there is no more statistics under his or her jurisdiction, which were approved by the Minister of Data and Statistics because the approval of production of statistics has been revoked under Article 19.
  (3) Where there is a revocation of designation of a designated statistics service agency under paragraphs (1) and (2), the designation under Article 17 or approval under Article 18 of the statistics which is produced by the relevant statistics service agency shall be deemed to have been revoked.

Article 17 (Designation of designated statistics and revocation of designation) (1) Upon receipt of an application from the head of a statistics service agency, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall designate any of the following statistics which are widely utilized for the formulation and evaluation of various government policies or for the production, etc. of other statistics as designated statistics: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Statistics which are produced covering the whole country;
  2. Statistics which become the basic data for the formulation of policies for regional development and for the evaluation thereof;
  3. Statistics that can be utilized as population data of other statistics;
  4. Statistics produced in accordance with uniform standards and the method of production which are recommended by an international organization, such as the United Nations;
  5. Other statistics recognized as necessary by the Minister of Data and Statistics to be designated as designated statistics.
  (2) If designated statistics cease to meet the requirements for designation under paragraph (1), the Minister of Data and Statistics may revoke such designation. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) When the Minister of Data and Statistics designates designated statistics or revokes the designation of designated statistics, he or she shall publicly notify thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) The procedure for and method of designation of designated statistics, and matters necessary for the matters to be included in public notice under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER IV PRODUCTION, DISSEMINATION AND USE OF STATISTICS

SECTION 1 Production of Statistics

Article 18 (Approval for production of statistics) (1) Where the head of a statistics service agency intends to produce new statistics, he or she shall obtain prior approval from the Minister of Data and Statistics on the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as name, kind, purpose, subject of survey, method of survey, statistical chart form, distinction of sex, etc. The same shall apply where he or she intends to change the approved matters or to suspend the production of statistics that has been approved. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The head of a statistics service agency shall determine in advance whether it is possible to produce statistics by utilizing administrative materials before he or she obtains approval under paragraph (1) or he or she holds consultations with the Minister of Data and Statistics under Article 20. In such cases, he or she may request the Minister of Data and Statistics to make a judgment thereon. <Added on Aug. 9, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) In any of the following cases, the Minister of Data and Statistics need not give approval under paragraph (1): <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where it is recognized that the details, such as the subject, purpose, method of a survey or report, are the same as or similar to those of other statistics that have been already approved;
  2. Where it is recognized that it is impracticable to ensure the reliability of statistics because the sample size is too small or proven techniques for producing statistics are not used;
  3. Where it is not recognized as being produced for the purpose of public interest because the subject, purpose, etc. of a survey or report give too much weight to a specific interest group or specific section or it is produced for profit.
  (4) When the Minister of Data and Statistics has given approval under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly notify thereof. In such cases, matters to be included in public notice, such as the title of statistics that has been approved and name of statistics service agency, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 19 (Revocation of approval for production of statistics) (1) If the statistics that have been approved under Article 18(1) fall under any of the following cases, the Minister of Data and Statistics may revoke such approval: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where the head of a statistics service agency fails to comply with a request for suspension of or change in production of statistics or with a request for improvement of business affairs relating to the production and dissemination of statistics, in violation of Article 12(2);
  2. Where the statistics fall under any subparagraph of Article 18(3);
  3. Where the statistics do not comply with the standard classification prepared and publicly notified by the Minister of Data and Statistics, or are produced by applying a standard different from the standard classification without obtaining approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 22(2);
  4. Where the statistics are remarkably underutilized in the formulation and evaluation of government policies or in the research and analysis of economic and social phenomena.
  (2) Where the statistics, the approval of which has been revoked under paragraph (1), are designated statistics, it shall be deemed that the designation of designated statistics is revoked simultaneously with the revocation of approval.
  (3) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall publicly notify when he or she revokes approval under paragraph (1). In such cases, matters to be included in the public notice, such as the title of statistics whose approval has been revoked and name of a statistics service agency, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 20 (Consultation on production of statistics) (1) Where the head of a statistics service agency produces statistics in accordance with any other statutes, he or she shall have a prior consultation with the Minister of Data and Statistics on the matters not prescribed by the statutes among the matters requiring approval under Article 18(1). The same shall apply where he or she intends to modify the matters that have been consulted or to suspend production of statistics that have been consulted. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) It shall be deemed to have obtained approval under Article 18(1) where it has undergone consultation under paragraph (1).

Article 21 (Advice to produce statistics) (1) If it is necessary to produce new statistics due to changes in economic or social conditions, the Minister of Data and Statistics may recommend such production to the relevant agencies, etc. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics may provide the personnel, technical support, and other resources necessary for preparing the statistics to the agencies, etc. that produce statistics in accordance with the recommendation under paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 21-2 (Request for production of statistics) (1) A person who intends to use new statistics may request the head of a statistics service agency to produce new statistics meeting all of the following requirements:
  1. There shall be a joint request by at least 20 persons who intend to use new statistics;
  2. The new statistics shall not be the same as or similar to the other statistics that have already been approved;
  3. The new statistics shall be deemed to have economic and social value according to the standard prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the possibility of being utilized as foundation data to formulate policies, etc.
  (2) The head of a statistics service agency shall examine the purpose of use, contents, etc. of new statistics according to a request under paragraph (1) and where he or she determines that they are reasonable, he or she may produce new statistics upon obtaining approval from the Minister of Data and Statistics under Article 18. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for procedures for making a request for production of new statistics, methods of examination, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 27, 2016]

Article 22 (Standard classification) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall prepare and publicly notify a standard classification concerning industries, occupations, diseases, causes of death, etc. on the basis of international standard classifications so that statistics service agencies may produce statistics according to the same standard. In such cases, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall have a prior consultation with the head of the relevant agencies. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) When the heads of statistics service agencies produce statistics, they shall follow the standard classification prepared and publicly notified by the Minister of Data and Statistics under paragraph (1); provided, when they intend to apply a standard different from any of the standard classification due to an unavoidable purpose of producing statistics, they shall obtain prior consent from the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) If it is necessary for the efficient production of statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the heads of public institutions to prepare, acquire, and manage administrative materials using the standard classification under paragraph (1). <Added on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) If the Minister of Data and Statistics determines that there is a risk that the contents of the standard classifications may be misrepresented because their contents are altered, summarized, or excerpted in published form, they may order the publisher to make corrections. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 23 (Cooperation in production of statistics) (1) Where necessary for the production of statistics that have been approved or consulted on under Article 18(1) or 20(1), the head of a statistics service agency may request cooperation to the head of a relevant statistics service agency. In such cases, the head of the statistics service agency who has received such request for cooperation shall comply therewith unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) Except as otherwise provided in other statutes or regulations, the statistics service agency that has requested for cooperation shall bear the expenses incurred in the cooperation under paragraph (1); provided, the agency that has been requested to provide cooperation comes to utilize produced statistics, they may share the expenses through mutual consultation.

Article 24 (Provision of administrative materials) (1) If necessary for the production of statistics, the head of a central administrative agency or the head of a local government may request the head of a public institution to provide administrative materials. <Amended on Apr. 1, 2009; Dec. 18, 2012>
  1. Deleted; <Apr. 1, 2009>
  2. Deleted; <Apr. 1, 2009>
  3. Deleted; <Apr. 1, 2009>
  4. Deleted. <Apr. 1, 2009>
  (2) If the Minister of Data and Statistics intends to establish a statistical register, he or she may request the head of a public institution to provide administrative materials. <Added on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) If the Minister of Data and Statistics deems it necessary for the production of statistics at the request of a designated statistics service agency prescribed by Presidential Decree taking into consideration the importance, etc. of statistics under his or her jurisdiction, he or she may request the head of a public institution to provide administrative materials. In such cases, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall, without delay, provide the relevant designated statistics service agency with the administrative materials provided, notwithstanding paragraph (7). <Added on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Where the head of a public institution is requested to provide administrative materials pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (3), he or she shall comply with such request unless there is good cause prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as infringement of State secrets, and of important secrets of individuals or enterprises. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Jul. 18, 2023>
  (5) Where the head of a public institution provides administrative materials under paragraph (4), the scope and method of provision shall be determined through consultation between the head of the requesting institution and the head of the providing institution. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (6) A person who is provided with administrative materials pursuant to paragraph (4) shall take technical and physical measures (hereinafter referred to as "information protection measures") necessary for ensuring safety in advance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to prevent loss, theft, or divulgence of the data received. <Added on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (7) No person who receives administrative materials pursuant to paragraph (4) shall use the materials for any purpose other than the production of statistics, or provide them to other persons. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (8) Where the head of an agency to be provided with administrative materials fails to take the information protection measures required under paragraph (6) or violates paragraph (7), the head of an institution providing administrative materials may suspend or limit the provision of such materials. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>

Article 24-2 (Provision of data by judicial agencies) (1) If it is necessary for the production of statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the Minister of the National Court Administration to provide computer data on the registration of family relations. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Where it is necessary for the production of statistics, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency and the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard to provide information on criminal justice related to statistics on the causes of death. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Article 24(2) through (8) shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters necessary for the provision of data under paragraphs (1) and (2). <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (4) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall produce statistics (hereinafter referred to as "vital statistics") to identify demographic changes such as birth, death, marriage and divorce, based on the following data: <Added on Dec. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Computer data on the registration of family relations under paragraph (1);
  2. Other data prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as data prepared and submitted by a reporting party at the time of reporting matters such as birth, death, marriage and divorce under other statutes.
  (5) The scope of data for which provision can be requested pursuant to paragraph (1) and matters such as the scope and method of conducting a survey for production of the vital statistics under paragraph (4) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Dec. 27, 2016>
  [This Article Added on May 14, 2014]

Article 25 (Request to submit data) (1) Where relevant data are necessary for the production of designated statistics, the head of a central administrative agency or local government shall judge in advance whether he or she may achieve the purpose of producing designated statistics by utilizing administrative materials provided pursuant to Article 24. <Added on Aug. 9, 2017>
  (2) Where it is impossible to produce designated statistics by utilizing administrative materials provided pursuant to Article 24, the head of a central administrative agency or local government may request individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. to submit relevant data. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017>
  (3) If it is deemed necessary for the production of designated statistics at the request of a designated statistics service agency, the Minister of Data and Statistics may make a request under paragraph (2). <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Any person who has received a request to submit data under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall comply with such request unless there is good cause. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020>
  (5) Matters necessary for procedures, methods, etc. for requesting to submit data under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017>
  [Title Amended on Aug. 9, 2017]

Article 26 (On-site investigation) (1) Where it is necessary to investigate or confirm matters approved by the Minister of Data and Statistics under Article 18 for the production of statistics, the head of a statistics service agency shall judge in advance whether it is possible to achieve the purpose of producing statistics by utilizing administrative materials which the relevant statistics service agency may utilize. In such cases, the head of a designated statistics service agency under Article 15 may request the Minister of Data and Statistics to make a judgment thereon. <Added on Aug. 9, 2017; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) If it is impossible to achieve the purpose of producing statistics by utilizing administrative materials under paragraph (1), a person who is engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics may request relevant persons to submit relevant data or ask them questions relating to the matters approved by the Minister of Data and Statistics under Article 18. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) In conducting investigation or confirmation for the production of designated statistics, those who have been requested to submit data or have been asked questions under paragraph (2) shall comply therewith unless there is good cause. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020>
  (4) Where it is necessary to conduct surveys or verification for the establishment and operation of statistical registers, the Minister of Data and Statistics may require persons engaged in business affairs relating to the establishment of statistical registers to request relevant persons to submit related data or to question them. <Added on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) A person who performs the duties under paragraph (2) or (4) shall carry identification verifying his or her authority and present it to the relevant persons. <Amended on Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020; Jul. 18, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Aug. 9, 2017]

SECTION 2 Dissemination and Use of Statistics

Article 27 (Publication of statistics) (1) When the head of a statistics service agency produces statistics, he or she shall publish the result thereof without delay, unless he or she otherwise fixes a date scheduled for publication. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016>
  (2) When the head of a statistics service agency publishes statistics under paragraph (1), he or she shall publish it along with necessary matters, such as the object and methodology of a survey so that users of such statistics may use the statistics accurately.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the head of a statistics service agency need not publish statistics where the produced statistics fall under any of the following cases; in such cases, he or she shall obtain prior approval from the Minister of Data and Statistics: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where it is recognized that considerable difficulty to the national security, maintenance of order or public welfare may be brought about if published;
  2. Where it is recognized that confusion in use may be brought about because the statistics are less reliable;
  3. Where there are substantial grounds to recognize the necessity not to publish the statistics.
  (4) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall immediately submit the details of and grounds for approval under paragraph (3) to the relevant Standing Committee of the National Assembly. <Added on Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) When the head of a statistics service agency deems that the reasons for not publishing the statistics under paragraph (3) have ceased to exist, he or she shall publish the statistics. In such cases, he or she shall have a prior consultation with the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (6) When the head of a statistics service agency discovers any errors in the contents of statistics published, he or she shall correct and publish them without delay. <Added on Mar. 26, 2024>
  (7) When the head of a statistics service agency publishes statistics under paragraph (1), (5), or (6), he or she shall submit the results to the Minister of Data and Statistics without delay. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Mar. 26, 2024; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 27-2 (Prohibition against exercising influence and revealing statistics with regard to production and publication of statistics, and against using statistics for purpose other than statistical purpose) (1) No one shall exercise influence over statistics staff (including persons engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics after being entrusted with all or part of such business affairs by a designated statistics service agency) for the purpose of changing the statistics being produced by a statistics service agency (referring to the statistics before being approved by the person of a statistics service agency having authority to grant approval and including information that describes the statistics and statistical data; hereinafter the same shall apply) or produced statistics (referring to the statistics approved by the person of a statistics service agency having authority to grant approval and including information that describes the statistics and statistical data; hereinafter the same shall apply) for the purpose of changing the statistics before publication or adjusting the date scheduled for publication without good cause.
  (2) No one shall provide others with statistics that are in the process of production or that have already been produced by a statistics service agency or reveal the statistics before publication of the statistics, or use the statistics for a purpose other than statistical purpose; provided, in any of the following cases, he or she may provide others with the statistics before publication:
  1. Where statistics being produced are provided to relevant agencies (referring to the agencies related to the industry, commodity price, population, housing, culture, environment, etc. being the subject of the statistics; hereinafter the same shall apply) and specialists to seek their opinions when new statistics are to be produced or existing statistics are to be changed, or where statistics being produced are provided to interested parties to open a public hearing;
  2. In any of the following cases, when a statistics service agency provides relevant agencies with the produced statistics:
  a. Where the statistics that are produced by simply aggregating administrative materials;
  b. Where a relevant agency requests to be provided with the statistics stating that they are in need of the statistics to perform duties;
  3. Where a statistics service agency is delegated or entrusted by another agency with the production of statistics and thereafter provides produced statistics to the agency that delegated or entrusted the production of the statistics.
  (3) Where a statistics service agency provides statistics produced pursuant to paragraph (2)2b to a relevant agency, it shall record the details, date, provider, method of provision, name of the agency being provided with the statistics and the person in charge at the agency, and keep the record accompanied by evidentiary materials for five years.
  (4) Where a statistics service agency provides statistics produced pursuant to paragraph (2)2b to a relevant agency, it shall provide the statistics to the relevant agency after noon of the day before the date scheduled for publication; provided, this shall not apply where Presidential Decree prescribes exceptions for international cooperation for which statistics are submitted to an international organization upon request, etc., or for cases in which taking countermeasures by a relevant agency is deemed urgent due to economic crisis, market instability, etc.
  (5) Where a statistics service agency provides statistics produced under paragraph (2)2b to a relevant agency, it shall disclose to the public the result (referring to the details of statistics, to whether the date scheduled for publication is to be changed and to reasons for change if any change is made) of comparison between, and examination of, the statistics produced in the previous year and the published statistics by March 31 of each year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and submit such result to the Minister of Data and Statistics. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Jan. 27, 2016]

Article 28 (Dissemination of statistics) (1) When the head of a statistics service agency publishes statistics, he or she shall take necessary measures, such as the construction of a statistics database, so that people may use them swiftly and conveniently.
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall devise necessary measures, such as the construction, linkage, and consolidation of statistics databases, so that the results of statistics, statistics publications and the details of publications submitted under Articles 27(7) and 29(2) may be provided extensively to users of statistics. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Mar. 26, 2024; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) If it is necessary for the construction, linkage, consolidation, etc. of statistics databases, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request for the submission of detailed statistical data, such as materials of the database that a statistics service agency keeps. In such cases, the statistics service agency that has been requested shall comply therewith unless there is any compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) When the head of a statistics service agency constructs a statistics database pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall be constructed under standardized statistical data classification codes. The standardization of statistical data classification codes and other necessary matters shall be determined by Presidential Decree. <Added on Apr. 1, 2009>

Article 29 (Issuance of statistics publications) (1) For the purpose of promoting dissemination of statistics, the head of a statistics service agency may issue or sell statistics publications (referring to publications that contain statistics and statistical data including those that use electronic media; hereinafter the same shall apply) firsthand or by entrusting them to other agencies, etc.
  (2) When the head of a statistics service agency has issued statistics publications prescribed by Presidential Decree, he or she shall submit the statistics publications and details of such publications to the Minister of Data and Statistics without delay. The same shall apply where the names or details of statistics publications are amended or he or she suspends issuance. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 29-2 (Keeping and management of statistical data) (1) The head of each statistics service agency shall keep and manage statistical data in order to encourage the dissemination and use of statistical data.
  (2) Matters necessary for keeping and managing statistical data, such as methods therefor, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 18, 2012]

Article 29-3 (Provision of statistical register data) (1) If it is necessary for the production of statistics, the head of a statistics service agency may request the Minister of Data and Statistics to provide statistical register data. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for the provision of statistics register data under paragraph (1), the Minister of Data and Statistics shall determine whether to provide the data, the scope of data to be provided, and other relevant matters in consultation with the head of the requesting agency. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) If information on corporations, organizations, etc. are included in statistics register data to be provided under paragraph (2), the Minister of Data and Statistics may provide the data in a form that identifies a specific corporation, organization, or similar entity. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) If the statistics register data to be provided under paragraph (2) contains information on individuals, the Minister of Data and Statistics shall provide such data after treating the statistical register data in a form that does not identify a specific individual; provided, if it is unavoidable to provide with a statistics service agency in a form that identifies a specific individual because the head of the statistics service agency requests it to use as a sample for survey, he or she may provide the statistics service agency in a form that identifies a specific individual. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) No person who is provided with statistical register data pursuant to paragraphs (2) through (4) shall use the data for any purpose other than that for which they are provided, nor shall provide them to other persons.
  (6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), matters necessary for procedures, methods, scope, etc. for providing statistics register data shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 18, 2023]

Article 30 (Provision of statistical data) (1) The head of a statistics service agency may request other statistics service agencies to provide statistical data if it is necessary for the production of statistics. In such cases, the head of a statistics service agency shall, upon receipt of such request, comply therewith unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) When the head of a statistics service agency provides statistical data to other statistics service agency pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall provide such statistical data after editing them in a form that does not identify a specific individual, or a corporation, organization, or similar entity; provided, where the head of other statistics service agency makes a request under paragraph (1) to use statistical data as samples for any of the following surveys, he or she may provide the statistical data in a form that identifies a specific individual, or a corporation, organization, or similar entity: <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012; Jul. 18, 2023>
  1. Survey for the production of statistical data after obtaining approval or undergoing consultations pursuant to Article 18(1) or 20(1);
  2. Preliminary survey for the production of statistical data after approval under Article 18(1) is applied or a request for consultation under Article 20(1) is made for the production of such statistical data.
  (3) The statistical data provided by a statistics service agency pursuant to paragraph (2) shall not be used for a purpose other than the purpose for which they have been provided, or shall not be provided to other persons.
  (4) Matters necessary for methods, etc. for providing statistical data shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Use of statistical register data or statistical data) (1) A person who intends to use statistical register data may request the Minister of Data and Statistics for the provision of statistical register data, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) A person who intends to use statistical data may request the head of a statistics service agency for the provision of statistical data as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Jul. 18, 2023>
  (3) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1) or (2), the Minister of Data and Statistics or the head of a statistics service agency shall review the validity of the purpose, contents, and scope of the intended use of the statistical registry data or statistical data, and shall provide such data if he or she determines the application to be valid and finds no likelihood of infringing trade secrets. In such cases, the Minister of Data and Statistics or the head of a statistics service agency shall provide statistical register data or statistical data after editing them in a form does not identify a specific individual, or a corporation, organization, or similar entity, except for the following cases: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where a statistical respondent requests the data to which he or she has responded;
  2. Where the following information, which includes business entities' names, business categories, and addresses as prescribed by Presidential Decree, is provided:
  a. Information contained in statistical registers;
  b. Information acquired through a census of business entities;
  c. Information acquired through statistics produced by method of conducting a complete enumeration of business entities.
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), where any of the following is applicable by comparing or cross-referencing the statistical register data or statistical data concerned with other data, the Minister of Data and Statistics or the head of a statistics service agency need not provide the statistical register data or statistical data: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where a specific individual, or a corporation, organization, or similar entities identifiable;
  2. Where trade secrets of a business entity are infringed.
  (5) No person who has been provided with statistics register data or statistical data under paragraph (3) shall use such data for any purpose other than that for which it has been provided, nor shall provide them to other persons. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (6) Matters necessary for methods, etc. for providing statistics register data or statistical data shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Jul. 18, 2023]

Article 31-2 (Establishment and operation of statistics data center) (1) The Minister of Data and Statistics may establish and operate a statistics data center to support the production of statistics by statistics service agencies and research, analysis, etc. by users of statistics (hereinafter referred to as "data center"). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics shall perform the following business affairs through the data center: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Provision of statistical register data and statistical data under Articles 29-3, 30, and 31;
  2. Education of users of statistics and consulting on the subjects or methods of analysis of statistical register data and statistical data;
  3. Other business affairs that the Minister of Data and Statistics deems necessary for providing support in the production of statistics by statistics service agencies and research and analysis by users of statistics.
  (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the establishment and operation of the data center shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 18, 2023]

CHAPTER V DUTY AND PROTECTION OF STATISTICAL RESPONDENTS

Article 32 (Duty of statistical respondents to answer faithfully) When statistical respondents have been questioned or requested to provide data, etc. for the purpose of production of statistics by a person engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics, they shall answer the matters of survey faithfully so that reliable statistics can be produced.

Article 33 (Protection of secrets) (1) Matters belonging to the confidential information of individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. that have become known in the course of producing statistics shall be protected.
  (2) Data belonging to the confidential information of individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. that have been produced for the production of statistics shall not be used for any purpose other than that of producing statistics.

Article 34 (Duty of statistics staff) A person who is or was a statistics staff member or who is or was engaged in business affairs for the production of statistics after being entrusted with all or part of such business affairs by a designated statistics service agency shall not use the matters that he or she has learned in the course of performing his or her duties for a purpose other than for conducting his or her business affairs, nor shall provide them to other persons.

Article 34-2 (Special cases concerning collection, use, and perusal of personal information) (1) Where it is inevitable to perform the following business affairs, a statistics service agency may collect personal information under the Personal Information Protection Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "personal information") to the minimum extent necessary and use it within the scope of its purposes:
  1. Business affairs regarding the establishment of the statistics register under Article 5-3;
  2. Business affairs regarding the production of statistical data after obtaining approval or undergoing consultations pursuant to Article 18(1) or 20(1);
  (2) Notwithstanding Article 20(1) of the Personal Information Protection Act, the head of a statistics service agency need not notify the data subject under the Personal Information Protection Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "data subject") of the matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 20(1) of that Act in any of the following cases:
  1. Where it is impossible to notify;
  2. In any of the following cases where it is significantly impracticable to produce statistics because it requires excessive efforts to give notification:
  a. Where personal information is collected to establish and operate a statistics register pursuant to Article 5-3;
  b. Where Personal Information has been collected to conduct a census pursuant to Article 5-4;
  c. Where personal information is collected pursuant to Article 24 (limited to cases prescribed by Presidential Decree for the production of designated statistics and other equivalent statistics);
  d. Where personal information is collected pursuant to Article 24-2;
  3. Where it is impossible to achieve the purpose of production of statistics or serious damage to statistics is likely to occur when the processing of personal information is suspended.
  (3) Notwithstanding Article 35 of the Personal Information Protection Act, in any of the following cases, the head of a statistics service agency may restrict or refuse the perusal of personal information by notifying the data subject of the reasons therefor:
  1. Where it is impossible to specify the personal information of the data subject;
  2. Where it seriously impedes the performance of statistics business affairs.
  (4) Notwithstanding Article 36 of the Personal Information Protection Act, if the correction or deletion of personal information seriously damages statistics in any of the following cases, the head of a statistics service agency may refuse a request for correction or deletion from a data subject by taking measures necessary to protect the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects:
  1. Where the personal information is collected to establish and operate a statistical register pursuant to Article 5-3;
  2. Where the personal information is collected to conduct a census pursuant to Article 5-4;
  3. Where the personal information is collected for the purpose of compiling designated statistics and other equivalent statistics prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Notwithstanding Article 37 of the Personal Information Protection Act, where the head of a statistics service agency is unable to perform any of the following statistics business affairs without processing personal information, he or she may refuse a request from a data subject to suspend the processing thereof:
  1. Statistics business affairs related to the establishment, operation, use, etc. of the statistics register under Article 5-3;
  2. Statistics business affairs related to the preparation, dissemination, use, etc. of statistics approved or consulted pursuant to Article 18(1) or 20(1).
  [This Article Added on Mar. 26, 2024]

CHAPTER VI SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 35 (Requests for submission of statistics) (1) Where it is recognized as necessary for the performance of the duties under this Act, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the heads of statistics service agencies for the submission of related data. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The heads of statistics service agencies that has received a request from the Minister of Data and Statistics under paragraph (1) shall comply therewith unless there is good cause. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 36 (Requests for correction of violations) (1) Where a statistics service agency commits any of the following violations, the Minister of Data and Statistics may request the head of the agency to correct such violation or to formulate a plan to take measures to prevent recurrence: <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023; Mar. 26, 2024; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where it fails to comply with a request for suspension of or change in production of statistics or a request for improvement of business affairs relating to the production and dissemination of statistics without good cause, in violation of Article 12(2);
  2. Where it produces statistics, or changes approved matters, or suspends the production of statistics that has been approved, without obtaining approval from the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 18(1);
  3. Where it produces statistics, changes consulted matters, or suspends the production of statistics that has been consulted, without consulting with the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 20(1);
  4. Where the statistics do not comply with the standard classification prepared and publicly notified by the Minister of Data and Statistics, or are produced by applying a standard different from the standard classification without obtaining approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 22(2);
  5. Where it fails to make publication of statistics, in violation of Article 27(1);
  6. Where it does not publish of statistics without obtaining approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 27(3);
  7. Where it publishes of statistics without approval of the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 27(5);
  8. Where it fails to submit the results of statistics, in violation of Article 27(7);
  9. Where, in violation of 27-2(3), it fails to record the details of produced statistics, which have been provided before publication, date of provision, provider, method of provision, name of the agency provided with such statistics, and the person in charge thereof at the agency, or fails to attach materials that can prove such record to such record, or fails to retain such records and materials that can prove such records for 5 years;
  10. Where it fails to disclose the result of comparison between, and examination of, the statistics produced in the previous year and the officially announced statistics, or fails to submit it to the Minister of Data and Statistics, in violation of Article 27-2(5);
  11. Where it fails to submit data, in violation of the latter part of Article 28(3);
  12. Where it fails to submit data, in violation of Article 35(2).
  (2) Where making a request under paragraph (1), if the other party to such request is the head of a central administrative agency or the head of a local government, the Minister of Data and Statistics may also request to give caution to or impose disciplinary action on the statistics staff members or related public officials responsible for the relevant violation. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Upon receipt of the requests under paragraphs (1) and (2), the head of the statistics service agency shall take necessary measures, such as correction of the violation, and formulation of a plan to take measures to prevent recurrence, or giving caution to or imposing disciplinary action on the statistics staff members or relevant public officials who are responsible for the violation, and shall notify the Minister of Data and Statistics of the results thereof. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 37 (Delegation and entrustment) (1) The head of a central administrative agency may partially delegate his or her authority to the head of an affiliated agency or to Mayors/Do Governors, or may entrust it to the heads of other administrative agencies or designated statistics service agencies as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Apr. 1, 2009; Dec. 18, 2012>
  (2) The Minister of Data and Statistics may delegate or entrust any of the following business affairs to an affiliated agency, or to an agency, etc. that conduct business concerning the development, promotion, and diagnosis of quality of statistics or business concerning the establishment and operation of statistical information systems, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Dec. 18, 2012; Jan. 27, 2016; Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Production of statistics (including surveys for the production of statistics) and public relation activities therefor;
  1-2. Establishment and operation of statistical information systems referred to in Article 7-2;
  2. Education of statistics referred to in Article 8;
  3. Execution of a regular examination of the quality of statistics referred to in Article 9;
  4. Business affairs relating to international cooperation under subparagraphs 1 through 4 of Article 14;
  5. Provision of statistical register data or statistical data under Articles 29-3, 30, and 31;
  6. Operation of the data center under Article 31-2;
  (3) The head of a statistics service agency may entrust any of the following business affairs to the Minister of Data and Statistics, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Added on Dec. 18, 2012; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Keeping and management of statistical data referred to in Article 29-2;
  2. Provision of statistical data referred to in Articles 30 and 31.
  (4) Where the Minister of Data and Statistics is entrusted with the business affairs pursuant to paragraph (3)2, he or she may re-entrust part of the business affairs that he or she is entrusted with to another agency, etc. that conduct business concerning the development, promotion, and diagnosis of quality of statistics, or business concerning the establishment and operation of statistics information systems with the approval of the head of the entrusting agency. <Added on Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 38 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) The executive officers and employees of the agency, etc. engaged in the business affairs entrusted under Article 29(1) and 37(2)1 (excluding public relation activities for statistics) and 3 shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions pursuant to Article 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>

CHAPTER VII PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 39 (Penalty provisions) (1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020; Jul. 18, 2023>
  1. Any person who exercises influence over statistics staff (including persons engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics after being entrusted with all or part of such business affairs by a designated statistics service agency), in violation of Article 27-2(1);
  2. Any person who provides others with statistics being produced or already produced statistics or reveals statistics before publication, or uses the statistics for a purpose other than statistical purpose, in violation of Article 27-2(2);
  3. Any person who uses matters classified as confidential information of individuals, corporations, organizations, etc., which are gathered or received (including the provision of statistical registers or statistical data under Article 31(3)) for the purpose of production of statistics, for any purpose other than statistical purpose, or provides them to other persons;
  4. Any person who peruses or is provided with matters classified as confidential information of individuals, corporations, organizations, etc. by deceit or fraud, which are gathered or received (including the provision of statistical register data or statistical data under Article 31(3)) for the purpose of production of statistics;
  5. Any person who alters or erases basic data, such as questionnaires gathered, kept, or managed by a statistics service agency for the production or dissemination of statistics, without good cause or who intentionally fabricates statistical data; provided, the person who corrects or alters any errors in a survey, entry errors, etc. in accordance with the procedures of examination of details or with the statistics service techniques inside the statistics service agency shall be excluded.
  (2) Any person who provides produced statistics before noon of the day before the date scheduled for publication, in violation of the main clause of Article 27-2(4), shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Added on Jan. 27, 2016>

Article 40 (Joint penalty provisions) If the representative of a corporation or an organization, or an agent or employee of, or any other person employed by, a corporation, organization or individual commits any violation provided in Article 39 in connection with the business affairs of the corporation, organization or individual, not only shall such violator be punished but also the corporation, organization or individual shall be punished by a fine under the relevant Article; provided, this shall not apply where such corporation, organization or individual has not been negligent in giving due attention and supervision concerning the relevant business affairs to prevent such violation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 41 (Administrative fines) (1) Where a statistics service agency fails to comply with a request for correction or a request for the formulation of a plan to take measures to prevent recurrence under Article 36(1) (limited to requests made due to violations of subparagraph 9 of that paragraph), it shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 5 million won. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (2) Any person who fails to comply with a corrective order, in violation of Article 22(4), shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 3 million won. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Jul. 18, 2023>
  (3) Where a designated statistics service agency fails to comply with a request for correction or a request for the formulation of a plan to take measures to prevent recurrence under Article 36(1) (excluding requests made due to violations of subparagraph 9 of that paragraph), it shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 2 million won. <Amended on Jul. 18, 2023>
  (4) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 1 million won: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2016; Aug. 9, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020; Jul. 18, 2023; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Any person who uses administrative materials (excluding the matters classified as confidential information) provided by a public institution for a purpose other than that for which he or she has been provided, or provides such materials to other persons, in violation of Article 24(7);
  2. Any person who rejects or obstructs the provision of data, or submits false data, in violation of Article 25(4);
  3. Any person who rejects, obstructs, or evades a request for submission of related data or for an answer, or submits false data or gives a false answer, in violation of Article 26(3);
  4. Any person who uses statistical register data provided by the Minister of Data and Statistics or statistical data (excluding the matters classified as confidential information) provided by a statistics service agency for any purpose other than that for which it is provided, or provides them to other persons, in violation of Article 29-3(5), 30(3), or 31(5);
  5. Any person who uses the matters (excluding the matters classified as confidential information) that he or she has learned in the course of performing his or her duties for a purpose other than for conducting his or her business affairs, or provides them to other persons, in violation of Article 34 (excluding where the person is imposed with a penalty pursuant to Article 39(1)2).
  (5) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Data and Statistics; and those under paragraph (4) shall be imposed and collected by the heads of central administrative agencies (in cases falling under subparagraphs 3 through 5 of that paragraph, by the Minister of Data and Statistics, if a person subject to an administrative fine is requested to submit data or is questioned by a person engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics at a designated statistics service agency, or is provided with statistical data by a designated statistics service agency, or is or was a statistics staff member of a designated statistics service agency, or is or was engaged in business affairs relating to the production of statistics after being entrusted with all or part of such business affairs by a designated statistics service agency) or by the heads of local governments, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Dec. 31, 2008; Jan. 27, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
